content.comment_body: Hello. I'm attempting to connect my device [article_no] to the internet. When I run a ping test to 8.8.8.8, I get a connection error. When I try connecting to cloud services, the [product_name] fails the test due to no internet. Are there specific ports or addresses I should open in my network? How can I confirm that [product_name] is online? My PC settings: IP: 192.168.1.87, Subnet mask: 255.255.255.0, Gateway: 192.168.1.254. Device configuration: IP: 192.168.1.210, Subnet mask: 255.255.255.0, Gateway: 192.168.1.254.

I've tested multiple ethernet cables and confirmed they are working. Ping from [product_name] to modem: successful. Ping from [product_name] to PC: successful. I disabled the internet provider's firewall, but still couldn't connect. Ping from [product_name] to 8.8.8.8: results in a ping error.

To verify the internet connection on newer [product_name] versions, you can use NTP. Adjust the [product_name] clock to be slightly off and run the NTP client, setting 91.189.91.157 (ntp.ubuntu.com) as the server, then enable NTP time synchronization.
Hi, You can find a list of required ports in the [product_name] manual. Make sure you use the manual appropriate for your device version. Hope this is helpful.
He was able to establish a connection to the device by opening port 8443. Thank you for the assistance.

analysis.insight_summary: The user struggled to connect their [product_name] device to the internet, encountering errors when pinging external IP addresses. Troubleshooting included checking cables, disabling firewalls, and adjusting network settings. Connectivity was only achieved after opening a specific port. The discussion emphasizes the need for clear and comprehensive documentation about network settings and connectivity testing for these devices.
analysis.user_expectations: The user expects the [product_name] module to connect to the internet without requiring extensive troubleshooting or unclear port configurations, and to pass connectivity and cloud service tests seamlessly.
